process.title: How an engagement works
process.intro: A clear, predictable path from first conversation to a running system.

steps.title: Introductory call
steps.body: We discuss your goals, existing systems and constraints, and whether we are the right fit.

steps.title: Technical assessment
steps.body: We review the current landscape and propose an architecture, scope and delivery plan in writing.

steps.title: Iterative delivery
steps.body: We build in short increments with regular demos, so you see progress and can adjust priorities early.

steps.title: Handover and support
steps.body: Documentation, deployment pipelines and knowledge transfer – plus ongoing support if you need it.

items.q: Who owns the code and the intellectual property?
items.a: You do. Source code, repositories, documentation and other deliverables are transferred to you, and the contract says so explicitly. We can also work in repositories and cloud accounts you own from day one.
Yes. If you need a non-disclosure agreement before sharing details about your systems or product, mention it in your first email and we will sign it before going into detail.

items.q: Which time zone are you in, and how do we communicate?
items.a: We are in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, on Eastern European Time – one hour ahead of Central European Time – so our working day overlaps with teams across the EU. We work in English or Bulgarian, by email and video calls, with regular demos during delivery and a cadence agreed at the start.

items.q: How do you price projects, and is there a minimum engagement?
items.a: We do not publish a rate card, because scope drives cost. A fixed-scope project gets a fixed price after the technical assessment, and a retainer is billed monthly for reserved capacity. The smallest engagement is the architecture and integration audit.

Our core stack is C# and .NET for backends and web APIs, SignalR and WebSockets for real-time communication, relational and time-series databases, and automated CI/CD pipelines. For integrations, we work with whatever your ERP, CRM, e-commerce or industrial systems expose – REST or SOAP APIs, webhooks, files or message queues.

items.q: Do you provide support after launch?
items.a: Yes. Every delivery ends with documentation, deployment pipelines and knowledge transfer. After that, you can keep us on a support or development retainer, or run the system with your own team.

items.q: Where is HDN Technologies based, and who do you work with?
items.a: HDN Technologies (Ейч Ди Ен Технолоджийс ЕООД) is a software engineering company based in Plovdiv, Bulgaria. We work with businesses in Bulgaria and across the European Union.

items.q: Do you have experience with real-time systems?
items.a: Yes. Over a two-year engagement completed in 2026, we engineered a real-time teleservice communication platform for the automotive industry, including bidirectional real-time communication between machines and backend services with SignalR. Client details are confidential under NDA.

whyUs.title: Why HDN Technologies: Standards, Ownership & Fit
whyUs.description: How HDN Technologies works: direct senior ownership, tested and documented delivery, your IP, a GDPR-aware EU partner – and who we are a good fit for.
whyUs.heading: Why HDN Technologies
whyUs.lead: HDN Technologies is a senior-led software engineering company in Plovdiv, Bulgaria. Many companies can write code. When you hire an engineering partner, what matters is knowing who is responsible, what you will receive, and whether the system will stay maintainable after handover. This is how we answer those questions.

standards.title: How we work
standards.intro: The standards we apply to every engagement, whatever its size.

items.title: Communication cadence
items.body: One technical point of contact – the engineer doing the work. We agree the cadence at the start, for example a short weekly status update and a demo at the end of each increment, with direct answers by email in between.

items.title: Code and IP ownership
items.body: You own the source code, repositories and deliverables. We can work in your Git organisation and cloud accounts from day one, so nothing is ever held back.

items.title: Documentation and handover
items.body: Architecture overviews, records of important design decisions, API documentation and runbooks are part of the deliverable – not an optional extra at the end.

items.title: Testing and CI/CD discipline
items.body: Automated builds, tests and deployments from the first weeks of a project. Every change goes through the same pipeline, so releases are routine rather than risky.

items.title: Security and a minimal attack surface
items.body: Least-privilege access, secrets kept out of source code, pinned dependencies and no unnecessary moving parts. Our access is removed when an engagement ends.

items.title: Data protection and GDPR
items.body: We are a Bulgarian company within the EU legal framework. We design data flows with data minimisation in mind and can sign a data processing agreement whenever we handle personal data on your behalf.

example.title: This website follows the same rules
example.body: It ships no JavaScript, loads nothing from third parties, sets no cookies, and passes automated accessibility, performance and security checks before every deployment. It is a small example of the standards we apply to client systems.

services.title: SignalR, .NET API & ERP Integration Services | HDN Technologies
services.description: Real-time systems with SignalR, custom .NET backends and APIs, and ERP, CRM and e-commerce integrations: problems solved, deliverables and typical durations.
services.heading: Services & capabilities
services.lead: HDN Technologies, a software engineering company in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, works in three areas – real-time systems, custom backends and APIs, and business system integrations – from the architecture to a documented system running in production.

items.title: Real-time systems & connected devices
items.summary: Live, bidirectional communication between machines, devices, backend services and the people who operate them – including telemetry, event-driven messaging and resilient connection state.
problems: Machines or devices in the field that must be monitored, diagnosed or serviced remotely
Status data that arrives too late to act on
Polling-based integrations that waste resources and still miss events
Connections that drop silently and leave systems in an unknown state
deliverables: A real-time communication layer built on SignalR or WebSockets
Telemetry data flows and event-driven messaging
Connection and device state tracking with diagnostics
APIs for dashboards, operator tools and other services
practices: Explicit, versioned message contracts between devices and services
Clearly defined behaviour on connection loss and reconnection
Real-time transport kept separate from business logic
Structured logging and diagnostics for connected clients
Design that accounts for many concurrent connections
items.duration: Typically 3–9 months for a new platform; a few weeks for an assessment or a focused extension of an existing one.

items.title: Custom backend engineering & APIs
items.summary: High-reliability .NET backends and web APIs for products and internal tools that off-the-shelf software cannot cover, with sound data models and automated CI/CD.
problems: A product or internal process that no standard software supports
An existing backend that is slow, fragile or undocumented
APIs that partners or front-end teams find hard to use
Releases that are manual, risky and rare
deliverables: Backend services and web APIs in .NET
Relational and time-series data models, with migrations
API documentation for internal and external consumers
An automated build, test and deployment pipeline
practices: Consistent API design with versioning and predictable error handling
Automated tests where they add the most confidence
Database schemas designed for the queries the system actually runs
Infrastructure and configuration kept in version control
Least-privilege access and secrets kept out of source code
items.duration: Typically 2–6 months for a new backend or API; ongoing through a retainer for further development and support.

items.title: Business system integrations (ERP, CRM, e-commerce)
items.summary: Reliable data flows between the systems your business depends on – idempotent synchronisation, webhook orchestration and modernisation of legacy interfaces – so the right data reaches the right place once, and on time.
problems: Orders, stock, prices or customer data copied by hand between systems
Scripts or plugins that fail silently and create duplicates
Replacing an ERP, CRM or shop would break existing interfaces
Nobody can say where a record came from, or why it is wrong
deliverables: Integration architecture and data mapping between systems
Idempotent synchronisation pipelines and webhook orchestration
Error handling, retries and alerts for failed messages
Modernised or wrapped interfaces for legacy systems
practices: Idempotent processing, so retries never create duplicates
One documented source of truth for each type of data
Failed messages are kept and reprocessed, never silently dropped
Contract tests against each connected system's API
Audit trails that show what was synchronised, when and why
items.duration: Typically 1–4 months, depending on the number of systems and data flows; a single integration can often be scoped as a fixed project of a few weeks.

caseTeleservice.title: Case Study: Real-Time Teleservice Platform | HDN Technologies
caseTeleservice.description: NDA-safe case study: how HDN Technologies engineered a real-time, bidirectional machine-to-cloud teleservice communication platform for the automotive industry.
caseTeleservice.heading: Real-time teleservice communication platform
caseTeleservice.lead: Real-time, bidirectional communication between machines in the field and central services – with HDN Technologies responsible for the core engineering.
caseTeleservice.overview: A platform that connects machines in the field with central services in real time, so they can be monitored and serviced remotely. HDN Technologies was responsible for the platform's core engineering.
challenge: Machines in the field and central services had to exchange data in both directions, in real time – telemetry flowing in, remote-service interactions flowing back.
Communication had to stay reliable across many connected machines, with well-defined behaviour when a connection is interrupted.
The data had to flow cleanly into APIs, services and databases that other parts of the business could rely on.

approach.title: Bidirectional real-time communication
approach.body: A SignalR-based real-time hub connects machines with backend services over persistent connections, carrying telemetry in one direction and remote-service interactions in the other.

approach.title: APIs and service integration
approach.body: Well-defined APIs expose the real-time layer to other services and applications, keeping transport concerns separate from business logic.

approach.title: Telemetry and data flows
approach.body: Data flows were designed as a whole – from the machine, through the real-time hub and services, into storage – so every piece of data has a clear path.

approach.title: Reliability
approach.body: The system was designed for continuous operation, with attention to the connection lifecycle, error handling and diagnostics.

approach.title: Database architecture
approach.body: The database design covers both operational data and the data produced by connected machines, structured for the way the platform reads and writes it.

approach.title: Complete CI/CD pipeline
approach.body: Automated build, test and deployment pipelines make releases of the platform's components repeatable.

scope: Real-time communication between machines and backend services with SignalR
caseTeleservice.outcome: Delivered over a two-year engagement and completed in 2026.
relevance: Remote monitoring and servicing of machines, vehicles or equipment
Industrial and IoT telemetry flowing into business systems
Live dashboards and operator tools fed by real-time data
Any system where many clients need a reliable, persistent connection to a backend
caseTeleservice.discussNote: We are happy to go deeper into the engineering approach in a call, within the limits of our confidentiality obligations.

sections.title: Visiting this website
paragraphs: This website is a static site. It sets no cookies, uses no analytics or tracking, and loads no fonts, scripts or other resources from third parties.

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, operated by GitHub, Inc. (USA). When you load a page, GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address in its server logs to deliver the site and keep it secure. Transfers to the USA rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Our legal basis is our legitimate interest in operating a secure website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

sections.title: Contacting us by email
paragraphs: If you email us, we process your name, email address and the content of your message to answer your enquiry and, where relevant, to prepare or perform a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) or based on our legitimate interest in responding to business correspondence (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
We keep this correspondence only as long as needed to handle your enquiry and any resulting business relationship, or as long as Bulgarian law requires.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access, rectify and erase your data, to restrict or object to its processing, and to data portability. To exercise these rights, email sales@hdntechnologies.com.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. In Bulgaria, this is the Commission for Personal Data Protection (Комисия за защита на личните данни, cpdp.bg).
